scopeReview: PSO-5.B.1–3: clustered, dispersed and linear rural settlement; metes/bounds, township/range and long-lot survey methods; interactions with agricultural land use, access and historical layers. Distinguishes residential arrangement from land division and records from geometric appearance.
varietyReview: Four original maps: compact farmhouse cluster, elongated frontage lots with linear residences, partial rectangular survey and an irregular deed-reference parcel. Additional equal-area/frontage calculation verified. Applied source/history/scale cases complete eleven, with all five skills and varied keys.
repetitionReview: Different map tasks interpret concentrations, access frontages, documentary survey references and landmarks. A partial grid is not mistaken for a full36-section township, and no irregular shape alone proves metes/bounds. No copied map, exact repeated stem or numeric-only clone; empirical difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Primary course/BLM survey descriptions checked; no published plat was copied. All parcels, corners, houses and dimensions are invented teaching examples, not legal property descriptions or guidance on a real dispute. Research remains QA-only; no new student resources or human-review claim.

questions.correctOption: Clustered or nucleated, because residences are concentrated rather than spread evenly across the farming area.
questions.independentReview: Checked all nine house coordinates lie within x64–76,y26–38, with variation on both axes rather than one line. Agricultural fields are external to the concentration; no origin cause or property system is inferred from the points alone. Mobile inspection moved the field label into its illustrated field by using a convex field outline; house coordinates and classification remain unchanged.

questions.correctOption: Narrow lots extending back from common river frontage can encourage houses to align near that access corridor.
questions.independentReview: Verified four elongated lots have a shared bank at y50 and houses share y40 within each parcel. The river is a frontage corridor, not a political border; no universal historical cause is inferred from alignment alone.

Verified BLM’s rectangular-survey terminology and nominal36-section township structure. The drawing is explicitly partial, near-square at rendering scale and not an exact real survey; no inference that every rectangular parcel worldwide is PLSS is made.

questions.correctOption: Metes and bounds using directions, distances and referenced landmarks or features.
questions.independentReview: Checked the deed’s explicit documentary features against BLM’s metes-and-bounds guidance. Polygon shape alone does not determine the method; no actual bearings are invented or presented as a legally valid closed traverse. The parcel boundary includes the intermediate creek vertex, so R–S follows the same plotted feature rather than a conflicting straight chord. Desktop light-mode inspection separated S and Creek labels from the boundary; the shared schematic creek bend was updated in both path and polygon.

questions.correctOption: Dispersed residences may require longer routes to serve scattered households, depending on roads and actual distances.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished a conditional service implication from an exact travel-time prediction. No universal density threshold, farmer income or mode of transport is inferred from dispersal alone.

questions.correctOption: Linear residence patterns can follow access corridors under more than one parcel-survey arrangement.
questions.independentReview: Used the supplied non-long-lot parcels as a counterexample to a necessary-cause claim. No particular national settlement history is inferred from the row alone.

questions.correctOption: Both have 4 hectares, but B has five times A’s frontage.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed both40000m² and divided by10000 to get4ha; frontage ratio5. Rectangular shapes and dimensions are explicit, unlike unscaled schematic parcels; no legal entitlement or actual resource value is inferred.

questions.correctOption: Successive settlement and administrative phases can leave more than one survey pattern in the same landscape.
questions.independentReview: Compared a layered-history hypothesis with unsupported uniformity and age claims. The answer calls for historical records rather than assigning exact origins from geometry alone.

questions.correctOption: Historical evidence about water access, institutions, security and land-use arrangements alongside the house distribution.
questions.independentReview: Separated pattern recognition from causal explanation. The supplied well/market/meeting place are candidate influences, not independently proven causes or a complete account of the village’s history.

questions.correctOption: Settlement form can evolve as access networks change, while older alignments may remain visible.
questions.independentReview: Checked temporal comparison rather than treating present geometry as the only valid pattern. Roads are a plausible supplied access influence, not a guarantee that every new residence follows one cause.

questions.correctOption: Survey geometry and residential clustering can coexist because they describe different features of the rural landscape.
questions.independentReview: Compared the two mapped layers rather than treating their categories as mutually exclusive. No actual cadastral right, zoning permission or uniform legal system is inferred.
